findings.explanation: low confidence.  Witness: Prop 5.3.10 only proves the existence of h ∈ H^2(X^φ) whose restriction to a smooth fiber is non-trivial; it does not prove the restriction is of type (1,1), integral, or ample. The paper's own 5.0.2/5.0.3 only says the image is generated by an ample class and is one-dimensional/spanned by an ample class, not that an integral class restricts to a positive multiple of it. For a hyperkähler X, the assumption φ̄ ∈ im d₂ gives H^2(F)^{π_1(B°)} one-dimensional; for X^φ, Prop 5.0.3 says the restriction map is either trivial or has one-dimensional image generated by an ample class. But a class in H^2(X^φ, ℚ) restricting non-trivially could restrict to a rational multiple λ times the ample class; λ could be negative or non-integral, and no argument in the text adjusts by an integral class to ensure λ > 0 (or λ=1). Thus the 'ample' assertion is not established by Proposition 5.3.10 alone; this is exactly the gap the claim flags, and the paper supplies no separate proof (Theorem C is asserted to follow immediately from 5.3.9 and 5.3.10). Note also the restriction is via f: X^φ 	o Y in Theorem D; but for Theorem C case 1 the statement of ampleness is independent and unsupported by 5.3.10 as written. Conclusion: the formal claim is correct—the additional ampleness assertion is stronger than what Proposition 5.3.10 proves, and the paper gives no intervening argument; hence the claimed 'immediately follows' is incomplete for the 'ample class' part. Location: Theorem C, case 1 (p3-4) and 5.3.11 (p24-8). Confidence: high.

evidence.text: Moreover, there is a cohomology class h ∈ H^2(X^φ) which restricts to an ample class on a smooth fiber.

findings.explanation: low confidence.  Witness: The period map is a biholomorphism in a neighborhood of Y_0 in M_Λ (Theorem B(2)). Hence we can find a family Y → 𝔻 of hyperkähler manifolds such that its image under the period map coincides with the image of 𝒳 → 𝔻. The period map is only a local biholomorphism, so its image is a one-sided/open neighborhood of Per(X_0); it is not automatic that the whole image of 𝒳 → 𝔻 lies in this neighborhood. What actually follows is only that the two families coincide on an open neighborhood U' ⊂ 𝔻 of 0 (where U' may be smaller than 𝔻), so domination of the period image of one family by the other is not automatic and must be clarified. In particular the strong statement “its image under the period map coincides with the image of 𝒳 → 𝔻” is not justified by Theorem B(2)/local Torelli alone. Later arguments then use this to claim V ⊂ U is open and dense and to compare the families globally (p15-1, p15-5), so the gap propagates. The local-Torelli step should be formulated on a possibly smaller disk/neighborhood around 0, and the coincidence of the period images should be established only there (or an additional argument to extend it to all of 𝔻 is needed). This is exactly the clarification requested in Claim c2: global domination by the period/deformation family is not automatic from the inverse function theorem/local biholomorphism property. Note also that the reference to “Theorem B(2)” appears to be a typo/mismatch: the local Torelli theorem is Theorem 4.3.4(2), not Theorem B(2). However, this is a typo and not the mathematical error; the mathematical issue is that a local biholomorphism gives only a one-sided neighborhood, so the claimed global equality of images under the period map does not follow without clarification.

evidence.text:
**Proof.** Let us apply the Global Torelli theorem (Theorem 4.3.4(3)) to some hyperkähler Shafarevich–Tate deformation of X. We obtain that there exists a hyperkähler manifold Y_0 deformation equivalent to X_0 whose period coincides with the period of X_0. The period map is a biholomorphism in a neighborhood of Y_0 in M_Λ (Theorem B(2)). Hence we can find a family  
𝒴 → 𝔻  
of hyperkähler manifolds such that its image under the period map coincides with the image of 𝒳 → 𝔻. For every t ∈ U ⊂ 𝔻, the manifolds X_t and Y_t are deformation equivalent hyperkähler manifolds whose periods coincide. Hence they are bimeromorphic (Theorem 4.3.4(3)). □

findings.explanation: low confidence.  Witness: The stated identification should involve the Tate twist of the integral local system: H^1(B, R^1\pi_* \mathbb{Z}(1)) \cong W_{\mathbb{Z}}/\mathbb{Z}\eta. As written, both sides are not naturally isomorphic: H^1(B,R^1\pi_*\mathbb{Z}) is the integral cohomology of the local system of integral classes of the fibers, whereas H^0(B,R^2\pi_*\mathbb{Z}) (not W_{\mathbb{Z}}/\eta) is the group of global cohomology classes restricting to fiber classes, and the quotient W_{\mathbb{Z}}/\mathbb{Z}\eta gives the cokernel of sending the class \eta to the local system of invariant fiber classes. The missing \mathbb{Z}(1) twist is necessary to match Hodge types (a (1,1)-class versus a (0,1)-component under the Hodge projection); without it the claimed equality is not the standard Leray/global invariant cycle identification. Because this identification is used in (5) to identify H^1(B,R^1\pi_*\mathcal{O}_X)/im H^1(R^1\pi_*\mathbb{Z}) with a quotient of H^{0,2}(X), the integral coefficient issue directly affects the isogeny in Theorem 2.2.7 and hence the density statement in Corollary 2.2.8 unless corrected with the appropriate twist/torsion handling. The paper itself later writes W_{\mathbb{Z}}/\eta and applies p without adjusting for this shift, so the stated equality is not correct as an integral statement; with the Tate twist and quotient by the image of eta it becomes the standard one (up to torsion/isogeny, which is all that is needed).

findings.explanation: low confidence.  Witness: The step 'Since the group space Pic^0(Y_b) is of finite type, the group <M_b> is of finite type as well' is invalid: a discrete (or even closed) subgroup of a finite-type group need not itself be of finite type in the abstract-group sense without showing it is finitely generated; e.g., Q ⊂ R or an infinite discrete subgroup generated by infinitely many independent elements inside a finite-type group can fail finite generation. Here one needs E_b finite-dimensional (Raynaud gives dim 0) and <M_b> discrete, which would give finiteness only if <M_b> is closed/finitely generated in Pic^0. As written, the inference finite type of the ambient group ⇒ finite type of the subgroup does not follow for abstract subgroups and is the gap. (Also note the underlying first concern is not an error: the codim >= 2 hypothesis does give h^0=1 for general points of Δ.)

evidence.text: to L on \( Y_b \). By Raynaud's theorem [Ray70, Introduction], \( E_b \) has dimension \( h^0(\mathcal{O}_{Y_b}) - 1 \) for a general point \( b \in \Delta \). The assumption that \( h^0(\mathcal{O}_{Y_b}) = 1 \) for a general point \( b \in \Delta \) implies that \( E_b \) is discrete for any fiber of \( \pi \) over a general point \( b \in \Delta \). The line bundle \( M_b := M|_{Y_b} \) is in \( E_b \) by the first property.

findings.explanation: low confidence.  Witness: In Proposition 4.8.3 the proof asserts 'By Corollary 4.8.2 it is enough to construct a class β ∈ H¹,¹(X) such that q(β) > 0 and β · c > 0 for any class c ∈ NE(X/Y).' The construction in [p17-13] pulls back a Kähler class from a bimeromorphic model and takes its (1,1)-part; bimeromorphism only preserves the cohomology lattice in H^2(X,Z) up to Hodge structure and does not transport the positivity condition q(beta)>0 or positivity on the Mori cone NE(X/Y) without additional argument. Corollary 4.8.2 requires that beta lie on X itself and satisfy its intrinsic positivity conditions; the quoted version does not verify this after only bimeromorphic identification. The sentence should note this missing step (or prove it directly), hence the claim is correct that the quoted criterion is applied where bimeromorphic identification alone does not preserve the class beta hypotheses.

evidence.text: Proof. As before, we denote by η the pullback of an ample class on B to X. If NS(X) ⊄ η^⊥, then X is projective (Theorem 3.0.7), and we are done. Hence we may assume that NS(X) ⊂ η^⊥. In this case NE(X/Y) = NE(X) by Lemma 4.4.1. By Corollary 4.8.2 it is enough to construct a class β ∈ H¹,¹(X) such that q(β) > 0 and β · c > 0 for any class c ∈ NE(X/Y).
